To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the French welfare state, like many others, is confronted with an increasing demand for long-term care (LTC).

(1) LTC is a new and complex social risk that is not well integrated into the French welfare state; (2) the current system is not adequate to meet the growing demand for LTC; (3) the political power of various stakeholders is a major obstacle to reform; and (4) the current political climate in France does not favour the adoption of any reform measure in the near future.
the French LTC system is in need of reform, but that the current political climate makes it unlikely that any reform will be implemented in the near future.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the French welfare state is able to adapt to demographic and socioeconomic change.
the following questions: What are the main features of the French LTC system, and what are the main challenges for its future?
how the financing of LTC services is likely to evolve in France in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no reform in sight.
France is in need of LTC financing reform, but that the reform process is stalled.
France has a LTC financing system that is neither sustainable in the long run nor adequate for the growing needs of the frail elderly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the French LTC system is in urgent need of reform, but that the political will and the capacity to enact a reform have been lacking.
the French LTC financing system is in a state of limbo.
the reform of the financing of LTC for the frail elderly is a “ghost reform”.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the political power of the social partners and the social security system is such that the reform process has stalled, and that the political debate has become polarized between the proponents of a new risk under social security and those who support a targeted subsidy for private LTC insurance, with the result being that no reform measure is likely in the short term.
the French political system is not able to implement a reform of the LTC system, which would require a consensus between the main stakeholders.
the French LTC system is a “ghost reform,” which is a system that has been in place since the mid-1990s but has been continuously debated, modified and improved without ever being fully implemented.
